recap.headline: WHITE MAMBAS WIN UGLY, PARTH CHOKES PRETTY
recap.subhead: Vishal never left the top three. Parth rented half the waiver wire to reach the final, then the magic ran out.
body: White Mambas never fell out of the top three, finished No. 1 and closed it out 7-4 over LeParth James. Vishal lost the points category almost every single week and did not care: protect the ball, block shots, hit free throws, collect the hardware.

LeParth James was 12th as late as Week 6. Then Parth rode Quentin Grimes, a waiver pickup, all the way to the final, including 125 points and 18 threes in the semis alone. He also owned the best player in fantasy, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and still lost the final. That takes skill.
Suggs to be you had the No. 2 seed and the luckiest record in the league, then lost a semifinal on free throws by three thousandths. Luck is a loan. It came due.

MehtaWorldPeace finished last and won the points category zero times. Not once in 18 weeks. RUM paid $105 for Victor Wembanyama, the priciest player in the draft, then made 13 moves all year. The lights were on. Nobody was home.

bubble.headline: Parth Rises From 12th, Arnav Falls Off a Cliff
bubble.sub: Who came from nowhere, and who coughed it up down the stretch.

cards.body: Dead last for three straight weeks and still 7th with six weeks to go. Then Parth ripped off a run to the 3 seed and rode the waiver wire all the way to the final.
In the top six for 10 weeks, out for 8, never higher than 4th. Finished as the 5 seed: never comfortable, never out, never worth fearing.
Sat 4th with six weeks to play. Then 5th, 7th, 8th, 8th. Arnav missed the playoffs entirely, then won the whole thing the next year. Rehab works.
Won the final week 9-2 and still finished 7th, after six straight weeks parked in 8th. The comeback started about a month too late.

20-7-11.headline: Parth Rents the Waiver Wire and Steals a Semi
body: On paper, this was Keshav's week. Assists were Suggs's best category all year, and Parth rarely won them. So Parth went shopping: Tre Jones, gone from his roster by season's end, dished 28 assists, and Quentin Grimes, a pickup, added 25 more with 125 points and 18 threes. Assists went to Parth by eight.
Threes, another Parth weakness, fell the same way. Grimes and Malik Beasley, a since-dropped rental, combined for 35 of Parth's 91.

Then the comedy. Parth cut Keldon Johnson mid-week, Keshav scooped him up, and Keldon chipped in 3 blocks and 3 steals against his old team. It didn't matter. Free throws decided it, .816 to .813. Three thousandths, and Keshav went home.

20-1-12.headline: White Mambas Win a Semi in Their Worst Category
body: White Mambas lost the points category 14 times in 18 regular-season weeks. theInfamous won it 14 times. So naturally, Vishal won points by 150 in the semifinal.
Anthony Edwards dropped 84, Austin Reaves 77, and Fred VanVleet hit 14 threes. White Mambas buried theInfamous from deep, 105 threes to 66.

John J fought back where he lives: offensive boards by 41, with Şengün grabbing 47 rebounds and Josh Hart 36. Steals and blocks finished dead even. Assists went to John J by three. It still came up one category short, and the one that killed him was the one he never loses.
